name: OS-eDRAM: IGZO/IWO 2T0C gain-cell memory IP on a U.S. 200mm foundry
wins_axis: standby power per bit (W/Mb at idle) and on-die memory density vs SRAM at mature nodes
buyer: Always-on edge-AI ASICs (keyword spotting, vision wake-up, sensor fusion) and DoD/onshore sensor ASICs on 130-65nm U.S. nodes that are SRAM-limited
us_manufacturability: SkyWater Bloomington MN (S130/S90) or SkyWater Fab 25 Austin TX (130-65nm), both 200mm; needs a new IGZO sputter or In2O3 ALD + O2 anneal module. Development could start at NY CREATES Albany (300mm) or Purdue (200mm oxide BEOL demonstrated Sep 2026).
who_is_already_doing_this: imec (2T0C program since IEDM 2020), Kioxia, IMECAS, Macronix (3D 2T0C), Georgia Tech/Shimeng Yu (IWO eDRAM), Notre Dame/Datta (IWO 2T), Purdue/Ye & Li (ALD In2O3 3-layer 200mm), SEL (DOSRAM / OS-LSI; dominant oxide-semiconductor patent estate). Competing embedded memories already at U.S. foundries: Weebit ReRAM (SkyWater S130), MRAM at GlobalFoundries.
fatal_flaw: No U.S. foundry offers an oxide-semiconductor module. Qualifying one costs ~$10-30M and 3+ years [ESTIMATE], and PBTI lifetime was only ~1 year vs a 5-10 year target (imec 2021). ASIC teams rarely design in a single-source, unqualified memory when SkyWater already offers qualified ReRAM. SEL's patent estate is a freedom-to-operate risk.
possible: yes - cells demonstrated on 300mm, oxide BEOL demonstrated on a U.S. 200mm line (Purdue)
profitable: marginal - royalties on low-volume 130nm ASICs are small; the real money needs a 28nm-or-better foundry partner
doable_by_founder: no - process-module development and reliability qualification are far beyond <$50k and a day job

name: Standalone IGZO 2T0C DRAM die on a depreciated U.S. 200mm line (commodity DRAM substitute)
wins_axis: none for commodity buyers (loses on $/GB, bandwidth, latency); refresh power only
buyer: (would be) industrial and legacy DDR4 buyers in the shortage, who will not pay ~12x DDR5 prices
us_manufacturability: SkyWater Fab 25 Austin (200mm, 130-65nm) technically could add IGZO tiers; 130nm litho is the binding constraint
who_is_already_doing_this: Nobody commercially at mature nodes; imec, IMECAS, Kioxia, SK hynix, and Samsung pursue oxide DRAM at leading-edge pitches
fatal_flaw: 130nm lithography gives ~120x lower bit density than 1b DRAM (0.0035 vs 0.436 Gb/mm2 with 4 tiers); stacking recovers only linear factors.
possible: yes - physics works (2T0C cells and 4-tier stacks are demonstrated)
profitable: no - $/GB 12x DDR5 price today, ~125x DDR5 cost

name: IGZO memory printed on idle display-fab glass
wins_axis: none for RAM; large-area and flexible form factors only
buyer: none for RAM (possible niche: flexible smart labels, which is Pragmatic's market)
us_manufacturability: None: the U.S. has no active-matrix TFT panel fab (Foxconn's Wisconsin Gen 10.5/Gen 6 LCD fab was never built); all oxide-TFT capacity is in Asia. Pragmatic's IGZO FlexIC fab is in the UK.
who_is_already_doing_this: Display makers (Sharp, LG Display, BOE, JDI) for backplanes; Pragmatic (UK) for flexible IGZO logic and RFID; nobody for RAM
fatal_flaw: Micrometer design rules => ~100,000x lower density than DRAM, plus no U.S. line exists.
possible: marginal - TFT memory on glass is feasible but useless as RAM
profitable: no

name: OCTRAM-class 4F2 IGZO-on-capacitor low-refresh DRAM as a U.S. second source
wins_axis: refresh/standby power (W/GB) at DRAM density
buyer: mobile/IoT and AI-server low-power DRAM buyers (via DRAM makers), not a startup's customers
us_manufacturability: Requires a DRAM capacitor process => only Micron (Boise ID, Manassas VA) in the U.S.; Nanya (Taiwan) is Kioxia's partner. Violates rule 3 for us.
who_is_already_doing_this: Kioxia + Nanya (OCTRAM); Samsung (4F2 VCT with reportedly IGZO channel, 2028 target); SK hynix (4F2 vertical-gate DRAM at VLSI 2026)
fatal_flaw: Needs a DRAM fab and Kioxia/Nanya IP, which is not offered for license; it is a T4 incumbent technology race.
possible: yes - for DRAM makers
profitable: no - not for a startup

name: License NEO Semiconductor 3D X-DRAM and build it in the U.S.
wins_axis: $/GB via density (if claims hold)
buyer: DRAM makers (NEO's intended licensees), not end customers
us_manufacturability: Needs a 3D-NAND-class fab; no volume 3D NAND fab operates in the U.S. [UNVERIFIED - from training knowledge]. NEO's PoC was fabbed at TSRI (Taiwan) with NYCU.
who_is_already_doing_this: NEO Semiconductor (licensor), Samsung, SK hynix, Micron, Kioxia, imec, IMECAS
fatal_flaw: Single-cell, company-reported PoC with no peer-reviewed array data; production needs a $10B-class fab. NEO pitches to memory companies, so the licensee seat is not available to a startup.
possible: marginal - a PoC exists but array/multilayer feasibility is unproven
profitable: no - not for us

name: U.S.-made HZO FeRAM family (1-16 Mb, rad-hard option) via SkyWater + Sandia
wins_axis: supply security (U.S.-made, trusted) + non-volatile fast writes + radiation hardness
buyer: Space/defense primes (satellite bus controllers, munitions/flight data recorders) and industrial/automotive event-data recorders wanting an onshore second source
us_manufacturability: SkyWater Bloomington MN (S130; DMEA-accredited trusted foundry [UNVERIFIED]) or SkyWater Fab 25 Austin (qualified by Cypress as an alternate fab for small PZT F-RAM parts, so the line has F-RAM history); Sandia MESA (Albuquerque) for rad-hard pilot.
who_is_already_doing_this: Infineon (PZT F-RAM incl. rad-hard; 130nm F-RAM transferred to TI Dallas; Fab 25 history), RAMXEED (ex-Fujitsu, Japan), TI (embedded FRAM MCUs), Sandia (HZO R&D), FMC (HfO2, Germany), Sony/Fraunhofer/NaMLab (HZO 1T1C research)
fatal_flaw: HZO loses to incumbent PZT F-RAM on the specs F-RAM buyers pay for: 1e11 endurance and 1-month retention at 85C (IEDM 2023, 1Mb) vs 1e13-1e14 and >100 years. Infineon's F-RAM is already partly U.S.-fabbed (TI Dallas; Fab 25 history), so 'Made in USA' is not a moat against it. The niche is ~hundreds of $M/yr [ESTIMATE].
possible: yes - 1 Mb HZO arrays exist; Sandia has 200mm FeRAM
profitable: marginal - small, incumbent-dominated niche with a reliability gap to close
doable_by_founder: no - T2 chip company with qualification burden

name: AlScN ferro-diode memory for 500-600C electronics (Penn/AFRL license + STTR)
wins_axis: operating temperature / survival in extreme environments (no incumbent RAM or flash works at 500C+)
buyer: AFRL and hypersonic/engine programs; aero-engine OEMs (health monitoring); downhole tool makers (oilfield services, geothermal); planetary-probe teams
us_manufacturability: Prototype at Penn's Singh Center for Nanotechnology, Philadelphia [external-user access UNVERIFIED]; scale on a U.S. 200mm line with AlN/AlScN sputter capability (MEMS/RF foundries or SkyWater) [UNVERIFIED which has AlScN today]; high-temperature ceramic packaging from U.S. hybrid houses.
who_is_already_doing_this: Penn (Jariwala, Olsson), AFRL (Moore), other SBIR performers on the AF/DARPA topics; SiC high-temperature IC efforts (NASA Glenn, others) [UNVERIFIED]
fatal_flaw: Tiny, grant-shaped market that easily becomes an SBIR mill (the mission bars grant farming). It also needs a high-temperature periphery (SiC CMOS) that barely exists commercially, and Penn may already have licensed or spun out the IP [UNVERIFIED].
possible: yes - devices work at 600C; arrays early
profitable: marginal - high ASP but very low volume; depends on DoD program pull
doable_by_founder: marginal - best founder-entry among device cards via STTR, but not an 18-month revenue path

name: Ferroelectric 'Optane-slot' persistent memory (NVDRAM-class HZO 1T1C NVDIMM/CXL)
wins_axis: non-volatility at near-DRAM latency (persistence)
buyer: in-memory DB and AI-checkpoint operators (hyperscalers)

fatal_flaw: Needs a DRAM fab plus a CPU/OS ecosystem. Optane lost ~$576M in 2020 alone and took a $559M impairment, and the one company able to build NVDRAM (Micron) never productized it.

wins_axis: non-volatility at DRAM-like speed (instant-on, no backup power)
buyer: industrial automation (PLC/CNC), medical devices, automotive event recorders

fatal_flaw: Zero control: FMC has no chip, its timeline is uncertain, and once it ships it will use established distributors. A one-person channel partner has no moat.

profitable: marginal - thin channel margins

buyer: MCU/edge SoC designers on 22FDX

buyer: Samsung / SK hynix / Micron fabs and U.S. research lines (Purdue, NY CREATES, Sandia)

profitable: marginal - real market if IGZO channels win, but incumbents are strong

name: Supercap-Killer PLP Kit (MRAM write-cache reference design)
wins_axis: lifecycle length and non-volatility of the write cache (no supercap aging), board area, PLP reliability — NOT $/GB
buyer: Tier-2 enterprise/industrial and rugged/defense SSD makers, computational-storage startups, RAID/HBA card makers, flight/data-recorder and PLC OEMs with 10-20-year field life
us_manufacturability: MRAM die: Everspin Chandler AZ (MTJ BEOL, co-located at NXP) on GF Singapore 28nm CMOS today; Microchip Fab 4 Gresham OR 200mm from 2H-2027 for lower densities. Board assembly at any U.S. EMS. Not fully U.S.-made at 1Gb density until a U.S. CMOS source exists.
who_is_already_doing_this: Everspin application engineering (gives reference designs free), IBM (in-house FCM), Phison (controller support), Broadcom/LSI RAID (Everspin journal MRAM since 2012), Marvell/Microchip SSD controller reference boards
fatal_flaw: Everspin and the controller vendors already give this engineering away to win sockets, and the number of new PLP designs per year is dozens, not thousands — a kit business likely caps below ~$1M/yr; plus an ITC exclusion order on Everspin STT-MRAM (Avalanche, 337-TA-1487, ~mid-2027) could interrupt 1Gb supply.
possible: yes — the mechanism ships today in IBM FCM5 and LSI RAID journals
profitable: marginal — real but small niche; Everspin captures most of the value
doable_by_founder: marginal — T1 and needs an EE partner; no fab, no chip design

name: DDR3-EOL Socket Swap to ST-DDR4 MRAM
subbranch: STT-MRAM as small-density DRAM replacement (industrial long-lifecycle)
wins_axis: non-volatility + supply longevity (U.S. vendor roadmap) for boards needing <=256 MB
buyer: industrial PLC, medical-device and rail-signalling OEMs with DDR3 EOL exposure
us_manufacturability: Everspin Chandler AZ BEOL on GF Singapore CMOS; board work at U.S. EMS
who_is_already_doing_this: Everspin FAEs; long-lifecycle memory specialists (e.g., legacy-DRAM die-bank suppliers) solve the same EOL problem more cheaply with last-time-buy stock or LPDDR4 respins
fatal_flaw: 30x $/bit gap, 1Gb max per MRAM die (a 1GB board needs 8 dies), and ST-DDR4 is not pin/protocol compatible with DDR3, so a respin to LPDDR4/DDR4 is cheaper for almost everyone.
possible: yes — parts exist
profitable: no — loses on $/GB by ~30x except in rare <=256 MB sockets
doable_by_founder: marginal — consulting-only form is T0 but needs an EE

name: NewSpace MRAM Radiation-Data & Upscreen Service
wins_axis: radiation tolerance + non-volatility + data/lot traceability (supply security for NewSpace)
buyer: LEO/GEO smallsat bus and payload makers (Astro Digital-type buyers, constellation primes), university cubesat programs, defense small-launch payload integrators
us_manufacturability: Parts: Everspin Chandler AZ Toggle line (onshore Toggle program under $40M DoW subcontract), PERSYST on GF CMOS + Chandler BEOL; testing at U.S. beam lines; screening at a U.S. test house (East Coast lab feasible).
who_is_already_doing_this: Frontgrade (ex-Cobham CAES, QML MRAM using Everspin IP), Avalanche Technology (space-grade STT-MRAM, UMC 22nm), Everspin's own HR line, NASA GSFC/NEPP (publishes free radiation reports), independent upscreen/test labs and COTS-space distributors
fatal_flaw: Credibility and competition from free data: NASA NEPP publishes radiation reports for free, Everspin/Frontgrade/Avalanche sell pre-screened space parts with heritage, and a non-engineer founder has no radiation-effects reputation buyers will trust.
possible: yes — standard industry practice
profitable: marginal — small, credibility-gated market
doable_by_founder: marginal — T1 with a rad-effects partner; data platform is the founder's lever

subbranch: Discrete STT-MRAM chips (fabless on foundry eMRAM)
wins_axis: non-volatility + endurance vs NOR/EEPROM (not vs DRAM)
buyer: industrial/automotive NOR/FRAM replacement sockets, FPGA configuration, storage PLP
us_manufacturability: Poor: foundry MRAM modules are at Samsung (Korea/Austin for logic only), UMC (Taiwan/Singapore), TSMC (Taiwan), GF 22FDX (Dresden). No U.S. 300mm MRAM foundry offering; Everspin-Microchip Gresham line is exclusive.

fatal_flaw: Crowded tiny market (the category leader books ~$17M/qtr of MRAM product) plus a live patent war (Avalanche v. Everspin ITC 337-TA-1487) — a new entrant buys litigation risk for a market already served.
possible: yes — Netsol did it in ~5 years
profitable: no — crowded, sub-scale, litigious

wins_axis: Nominal $/GB vs 2026 DDR5 spot plus process simplicity. It wins on no axis once DRAM prices normalize.
buyer: Hypothetical legacy DDR3/DDR4 industrial buyers; SoC teams wanting dense LLC on SOI.
us_manufacturability: A U.S. GlobalFoundries SOI line (Malta NY / Essex VT; which SOI flows run in the U.S. in 2026 is [UNVERIFIED-training]) under a JDA. GF offers no capacitor-less DRAM today, and A3 knows no U.S. line running one.
who_is_already_doing_this: Nobody in Si floating-body production. Micron reportedly holds the ISi Z-RAM patents [UNVERIFIED-training]. NEO Semiconductor (3D X-DRAM, see C-05) and Unisantis (Dynamic Flash Memory) [UNVERIFIED-training] are the capacitor-less revivals. Samsung and SK hynix publish capacitor-less 3D DRAM research.
fatal_flaw: Physics at scale: body charge is a few hundred electrons at 45nm and tens in thin FD-SOI, so sense margin, retention and disturb immunity collapse with variability. AMD and Hynix both licensed Z-RAM and dropped it (2006-2010) [UNVERIFIED-training].
possible: marginal — demonstrated in test chips 15-20 years ago, never qualified; scaling makes it harder
profitable: no — 14x density gap vs 1b DRAM; ~$24/GB vs glut ~$11/GB

name: Thyristor RAM revival (T-RAM TCCT / Kilopass VLT)
wins_axis: Read latency (SRAM-class) and density vs SRAM. It does not win on $/GB vs DRAM except in the never-demonstrated VLT claim.
buyer: SoC cache designers (if it worked); hypothetical DRAM buyers.
us_manufacturability: A GF U.S. SOI flow or SkyWater Bloomington MN 90nm FD-SOI [UNVERIFIED-training]. Neither offers a thyristor module.
who_is_already_doing_this: Nobody commercially. GF dropped T-RAM. Synopsys owns the Kilopass assets and has not marketed VLT [UNVERIFIED-training]. There is some academic TCAD work on 3D thyristor DRAM.
fatal_flaw: The ON state needs a holding current. At 1-100 pA/cell a 1 Gb array idles at ~1-110 mA, and the bistable window shrinks at 85-125C. Three serious attempts failed to productize: AMD 2006, GlobalFoundries 2009, Kilopass 2016 [UNVERIFIED-training].
possible: marginal — TCCT arrays demonstrated, temperature/standby problems unsolved
profitable: no

name: Si gain-cell eDRAM (GCRAM) IP for U.S. trailing-node SoCs
subbranch: Capacitor-less silicon DRAM: 2T/3T gain-cell eDRAM in logic
wins_axis: On-chip memory density (bits/mm2) and standby leakage per bit vs 6T SRAM at equal process cost.
buyer: Edge-AI and sensor SoC teams on U.S. trailing nodes; DoD trusted-foundry ASIC programs; FPGA vendors needing denser block RAM.
us_manufacturability: SkyWater Bloomington MN (S130, 90nm FD-SOI) and Fab 25 Austin TX; GlobalFoundries Fab 8 Malta NY (12LP+). Test chips go via ChipFoundry/SkyWater MPW shuttles.
who_is_already_doing_this: RAAAM Memory Technologies (Israel; GCRAM, claims ~2x SRAM density) [UNVERIFIED-training]; academic groups at Bar-Ilan, EPFL and Georgia Tech (oxide 3T); Synopsys/Arm SRAM compilers as incumbents. C-01 covers oxide (IGZO) gain cells; this card is Si-only and zero-mask.
fatal_flaw: At 85-125C Si gain-cell retention is ~10-100 us, so refresh erodes the power advantage. Royalties at trailing nodes are small; the MoSys 1T-SRAM precedent saw modest royalties, then decline [UNVERIFIED-training]. RAAAM got there first.
possible: yes — silicon-proven in academia and at one startup
profitable: marginal — high-margin IP but small trailing-node royalty pool and an incumbent startup
doable_by_founder: marginal — needs a circuit cofounder and ~$2-3M

name: OpenRAM macro service for U.S. open-PDK tapeouts (SkyWater S130)
subbranch: SRAM-at-scale on trailing nodes: on-chip memory supply for U.S.-fab ASICs
wins_axis: Supply security and access: time and cost to get characterized on-chip RAM in a U.S.-fabbed ASIC. Not $/GB.
buyer: University VLSI labs, DoD SBIR/STTR ASIC teams needing U.S.-only fabrication, hardware startups on ChipFoundry/SkyWater shuttles.
us_manufacturability: Customer silicon is made at SkyWater Bloomington MN (S130) via ChipFoundry MPW, later SkyWater Fab 25 Austin. The venture itself is software in the U.S.
who_is_already_doing_this: VLSIDA/UC Santa Cruz (OpenRAM maintainers, free); ChipFoundry marketplace vendors; commercial compilers from Synopsys and Arm (not offered for open PDKs at small-team prices) [UNVERIFIED-training]; SkyWater's own IP partners.
fatal_flaw: Tiny market (MPW customers number in the hundreds per year) with low willingness to pay for something free (BSD). UCSC, SkyWater or ChipFoundry could bundle equivalent macros at no charge. It is also on-chip memory IP, not 'RAM' in the mission's main sense.
possible: yes — compiler and PDK exist; needs larger, better-characterized macros
profitable: marginal — likely <$1M ARR ceiling unless it expands to gain-cell IP (C-32) or more PDKs
doable_by_founder: yes — T0, software-led, starts alongside the day job

name: Depreciated-fab revival of IBM-heritage deep-trench eDRAM
subbranch: 1T1C eDRAM at foundries; depreciated trailing-edge capacity
wins_axis: Latency (~2 ns macro cycle) vs commodity DRAM. Nothing on $/GB.
buyer: HPC/ASIC teams wanting a fast on-package cache tier (hypothetical).
us_manufacturability: onsemi East Fishkill NY (ex-IBM 300mm; now running onsemi products) or GF Fab 8 Malta NY. A3 knows of no current U.S. deep-trench eDRAM capability [UNVERIFIED-training].
who_is_already_doing_this: Nobody. IBM exited eDRAM with POWER10/z16. Intel ended Crystalwell-class eDRAM. GF no longer offers 14HP [UNVERIFIED-training].
fatal_flaw: Depreciation cannot close a 17x density gap: wafer cost is a minor term once density is 0.026 vs 0.436 Gb/mm2. The tool set and know-how are likely gone [UNVERIFIED-training].
possible: marginal — it shipped before, but the process is retired
profitable: no — density gap dominates even at cash-cost wafers

name: Trailing-node bulk SRAM as a DRAM substitute (SRAM-DIMM/CXL)
wins_axis: None at a DRAM interface: the latency advantage is lost behind the DDR/CXL controller (~50-100 ns), and it loses on $/GB by 3-40x.
buyer: None identified. A DRAM buyer will not pay 4x spot for refresh-free capacity.
us_manufacturability: GF Fab 8 Malta NY (12/14nm) is the closest U.S. option. 28nm SRAM die is otherwise Taiwan-made.
who_is_already_doing_this: Nobody sells SRAM as bulk DRAM capacity. SRAM capacity is sold only as on-die memory (Groq, Cerebras, see C-38/C-39) or small standalone parts (C-36).
fatal_flaw: SRAM has a ~$80-120/GB silicon+test cost floor at every node from 28nm to N2. SRAM cell scaling has stalled, so trailing nodes are not cheaper per SRAM bit: 40nm is ~$144/GB and 65nm ~$268/GB.
possible: yes — trivially manufacturable
profitable: no — 4x above today's spot, ~10x above glut

name: U.S.-fabbed long-lifecycle SRAM second source (SkyWater Fab 25)
subbranch: SRAM 'RAM' products on depreciated U.S. 200mm capacity
wins_axis: Supply security and lifecycle length: U.S.-fab, 20-year availability, non-PRC ownership. Not $/GB.
buyer: Defense primes (avionics, radar, EW), DMSMS/obsolescence programs, industrial controls, networking line cards using QDR SRAM.
us_manufacturability: SkyWater Fab 25 Austin TX (200mm, 130-65nm) and SkyWater Bloomington MN (S130; 90nm FD-SOI for rad-tolerant parts [UNVERIFIED-training]); a U.S. hi-rel OSAT for assembly and test.
who_is_already_doing_this: Infineon (ex-Cypress SRAM; U.S. supply now via SkyWater), Renesas, ISSI (Ingenic-owned), GSI Technology (TSMC-fabbed high-speed SRAM), Alliance Memory, Rochester Electronics (EOL continuation, Newburyport MA). Rad-hard: Honeywell (Plymouth MN), BAE Systems (Manassas VA), Frontgrade [UNVERIFIED-training for current product status].
fatal_flaw: The incumbent (Infineon, supplied from the same Fab 25 under contract) and Renesas can match or undercut on any socket. The standalone SRAM market is small and shrinking, and qualification takes 2-3 years before revenue.
possible: yes — mature technology at a willing U.S. foundry
profitable: marginal — real margins per part, but a small market with a strong incumbent at the same fab

name: Compute-in-SRAM vector-search appliance on GSI Gemini APU
subbranch: SRAM-at-scale: compute-in-SRAM as a DRAM-bandwidth substitute
wins_axis: Watts per query and DRAM GB per QPS for large-scale vector search.
buyer: Air-gapped defense/intelligence RAG deployments; on-prem enterprise search with power or DRAM constraints.
us_manufacturability: APU silicon is TSMC (Taiwan) and boards are GSI-sourced. Integration and software are in the U.S., so the product is U.S.-assembled, not U.S.-made.
who_is_already_doing_this: GSI Technology itself (Leda boards, software); GPU/CPU vector search (NVIDIA cuVS, Milvus/Zilliz, Pinecone, Weaviate); other compute-in-SRAM startups (d-Matrix for LLMs, Areanna historically).
fatal_flaw: Single-supplier dependency on a small, loss-making vendor whose roadmap or survival is uncertain [UNVERIFIED-training], while GPU/CPU vector search improves every year and DRAM gets cheap in the glut.
possible: yes — the APU ships
profitable: marginal — thin hardware margin, vendor risk
doable_by_founder: marginal — software-led but needs a hardware partner that stays alive

name: Memory-only wafer-scale SRAM ('Cerebras for RAM')
subbranch: Wafer-scale SRAM as a RAM product
wins_axis: None for a host: on-wafer bandwidth cannot leave the wafer through an ~860 mm perimeter.
buyer: None identified. Latency-critical buyers buy Cerebras/Groq compute instead.
us_manufacturability: GF Fab 8 Malta NY for wafers. Wafer-scale packaging capability in the U.S. is unclear [UNVERIFIED-training].
who_is_already_doing_this: Cerebras (compute + SRAM on one wafer, TSMC). Nobody sells memory-only wafers.
fatal_flaw: Cerebras's economics come from co-locating compute with SRAM. A memory-only wafer exports its bandwidth through edge I/O, so it is DRAM at 40-100x the price with no latency advantage visible to the host.
possible: yes — engineering-feasible
profitable: no

name: U.S.-fabbed SRAM-only LLM inference accelerator (Groq pattern)
wins_axis: Tokens/s/user (decode latency) and energy per bit moved (no off-chip DRAM I/O).
buyer: Latency-sensitive inference (agents, voice, real-time trading) and sovereign/U.S.-made AI clouds.
us_manufacturability: GlobalFoundries Fab 8 Malta NY (12LP+/14nm), the same U.S. fab class Groq v1 used [UNVERIFIED-training]. U.S. OSAT assembly.
who_is_already_doing_this: Groq (with NVIDIA license), Cerebras, d-Matrix, SambaNova, Etched, MatX, Positron. Graphcore (now SoftBank) and Untether AI (team absorbed by AMD, 2025) [UNVERIFIED-training] show the attrition.
fatal_flaw: Upper-T3 capital (incumbents raised $0.3-1B+ each) against four or more well-funded incumbents, with NVIDIA now holding Groq's technology license. A 70B 8-bit model needs ~300+ SRAM dies.
possible: yes — shipping at incumbents
profitable: marginal — only for the category winner

name: Nantero NRAM (carbon-nanotube) license and U.S. second source
wins_axis: Non-volatility plus radiation and temperature tolerance (space/defense). Not $/GB vs DRAM.
buyer: Space primes and rad-hard component distributors (Frontgrade-type channel); downhole/high-temperature industrial.
us_manufacturability: SkyWater Bloomington MN (S130 BEOL) or Fab 25 Austin. The licensor is in Massachusetts (East Coast).
who_is_already_doing_this: Nantero (licensor; activity in 2024-2026 unverified). Fujitsu/Mie Fujitsu (licensees; Mie fab now USJC) [UNVERIFIED-training]. Rad-hard NVM incumbents: Everspin Toggle MRAM via Frontgrade, Infineon rad-hard F-RAM.
fatal_flaw: 20+ years and >$100M [UNVERIFIED-training] without a known volume product; the Fujitsu-licensed product apparently never shipped. In rad-hard it must displace qualified Toggle MRAM and F-RAM incumbents.
possible: marginal — demonstrated by licensees, never productized
profitable: no — no evidence of a cost or performance win that incumbents can't match

name: 2D-material (MoS2/WSe2) gain-cell DRAM or 2D flash
wins_axis: Retention per area (speculative) — not demonstrated at array scale.
buyer: None until TRL 6+.
us_manufacturability: No U.S. production line; research only (Penn State 2DCC, NY CREATES Albany).
who_is_already_doing_this: Academic groups (Fudan, Penn State, MIT, Stanford); TSMC/imec/Intel 2D-channel logic research [UNVERIFIED-training].
fatal_flaw: No defect-controlled, wafer-scale 2D growth at BEOL-compatible temperature, and no array-scale demonstration. Contact resistance and variability are unsolved. IGZO (C-01..04) already delivers the low-leakage benefit on 300mm today.
possible: no (not within the venture horizon) — lab devices only; UNSUPPORTED at array scale
profitable: no

name: Printed organic ferroelectric memory (Thinfilm post-mortem)
wins_axis: Cost per label for a few bits (anti-counterfeit tags) — not any RAM axis.
buyer: None for RAM; brand-protection labels at most.
us_manufacturability: NextFlex pilot lines (San Jose CA) or university printed-electronics labs. The former Thinfilm/Kovio San Jose line is closed [UNVERIFIED-training].
who_is_already_doing_this: Nobody for RAM. Thinfilm exited memory.
fatal_flaw: Density, latency and endurance are each 6-10 orders of magnitude from RAM. The company that pioneered it abandoned memory twice and later failed [UNVERIFIED-training].
possible: no as RAM (UNSUPPORTED for any RAM role; 20-bit labels did ship, no URL retrievable this session)
profitable: no

name: Cryo-CMOS gain-cell eDRAM IP for quantum-computer control
wins_axis: Static power at the 4 K stage and memory density for cryo control electronics.
buyer: Quantum computing hardware teams (IBM Quantum NY, Google Quantum AI), DARPA/IARPA quantum programs.
us_manufacturability: GF Fab 8 Malta NY (12LP+) or SkyWater Bloomington MN (90nm FD-SOI). Cryo test needs a dilution refrigerator, rented from a university or national lab.
who_is_already_doing_this: Intel (Horse Ridge), IBM Quantum, Google Quantum AI and imec do in-house cryo-CMOS; SEEQC (Elmsford NY) does superconducting SFQ control; academic cryo gain-cell groups [UNVERIFIED-training].
fatal_flaw: The market is a few dozen teams, most of which design memory in-house. Quantum roadmaps may keep control at room temperature for years. It needs a cryo test lab and a circuit designer.
possible: yes — physics favorable
profitable: marginal — tiny market

name: DDR4 Second-Life CXL Expander
subbranch: CXL memory expansion / DIMM reuse (Microsoft-Meta style DDR4 recycling)
wins_axis: $/GB of added capacity from already-owned DIMMs; lifecycle length/Scope-3; supply security when DDR5 allocation is refused
buyer: Tier-2/neocloud and large-enterprise operators with >=10k retired DDR4 RDIMMs and DDR5-only new servers (VM density, in-memory DB capacity tier)
us_manufacturability: Board assembly/test at any U.S. EMS (Sanmina, Kimball, SMTC). The controller silicon is TSMC (Taiwan). DIMMs are recovered from U.S. data centers. Only assembly and recovery are U.S.
who_is_already_doing_this: Marvell (Structera X: DDR4 support, inline LZ4) [UNVERIFIED-T]; Astera Labs (Leo; Azure CXL instances) [UNVERIFIED-T]; Montage (MXC); Microchip (SMC 2000); SMART Modular/Penguin Solutions (4- and 8-DIMM CXL AICs) [UNVERIFIED-T]; Microsoft and Meta in-house DDR4 reuse programs [UNVERIFIED-T]
fatal_flaw: At small-vendor volume the card costs ~$2.3/GB. The owner's DDR4 is worth ~$21-44/GB at chip spot in Aug 2026, and DDR4 is dearer than DDR5 in some channels, so 'sell the DDR4, buy DDR5' beats reuse. The arbitrage exists only at hyperscaler scale, where buyers go direct to Marvell/Astera.
possible: yes: deployed at hyperscalers with merchant controllers
profitable: no: computed negative unit advantage for a small vendor in trough, shortage and glut
doable_by_founder: no: hardware/firmware team and controller allocation required

name: KV Pool Node (shared DRAM+CXL KV-cache appliance)
subbranch: LLM inference KV-cache tiering - DRAM/CXL tier
wins_axis: $/GB-month of shared hot-KV capacity against GPU HBM (~$180-250/GB effective) and TTFT on cache hits
buyer: Neocloud inference providers and enterprise private-inference teams with long system prompts, RAG and multi-turn agent sessions
us_manufacturability: Integration/burn-in on a U.S. bench (East Coast) or through Supermicro San Jose. CPUs, NICs and most DDR5 are imported. Micron Idaho DDR5 is not before mid-2027.
who_is_already_doing_this: NVIDIA (Dynamo KVBM; Inference Context Memory Storage on BlueField-4 [UNVERIFIED-T]); WEKA Augmented Memory Grid (NVIDIA partnership Nov 2025); VAST Data; Pliops; Hammerspace Tier 0; Penguin Solutions (CXL KV server) [UNVERIFIED-T]; Enfabrica EMFASYS (now NVIDIA) [UNVERIFIED-T]; Moonshot/Mooncake in-house; Tensormesh (LMCache commercial)
fatal_flaw: No moat: a commodity server plus open-source software (Mooncake/LMCache) that Dell/Supermicro/NVIDIA reference designs replicate. A 4 TB node ties up ~$80-130k of DRAM at 4Q26 prices for a reseller-grade margin, and flash KV tiers take the warm data.
possible: yes: production at Moonshot; all parts off-the-shelf
profitable: marginal: VAR-grade hardware margin unless a subscription attaches
doable_by_founder: marginal: needs customer prepayment or financing for DRAM inventory

name: Flash KV Accelerator (U.S. Pliops-style NVMe KV engine)
subbranch: LLM inference KV-cache tiering - flash tier with hardware KV engine
wins_axis: $/GB-month of warm KV and TTFT on long-context reuse
buyer: Inference providers and enterprise RAG/agent platforms with long shared prefixes
us_manufacturability: FPGA silicon from TSMC. Board assembly at a U.S. EMS. SSD NAND comes from Micron (Singapore), Kioxia/SanDisk (Japan) and Solidigm (China fab). Little U.S. content.
who_is_already_doing_this: Pliops (XDP LightningAI) [UNVERIFIED-T]; WEKA (Augmented Memory Grid, NVIDIA partner); VAST Data; DDN; Hammerspace; NVIDIA ICMS/BlueField-4 [UNVERIFIED-T]; DeepSeek 3FS (open source; an LMCache backend); NVIDIA GDS + plain NVMe via Dynamo KVBM
fatal_flaw: NVIDIA is building this tier itself (Dynamo KVBM + GDS + BlueField-4 storage), and software-only stacks on plain NVMe (3FS, LMCache, HiCache) capture most of the benefit without a special card. A late U.S. entrant faces Pliops/WEKA/VAST with a 2-3 year head start.
possible: yes: shipping from several vendors
profitable: marginal: crowded and being absorbed by NVIDIA reference stacks

name: Compressed CXL Expander (licensed inline compression IP)
wins_axis: Effective $/GB (capacity multiplier) for compressible in-memory data
buyer: In-memory cache operators (Redis/Valkey/Memcached fleets) and VM hosts with cold pages
us_manufacturability: FPGA from TSMC; board at a U.S. EMS; IP from Sweden. Little U.S. content beyond assembly.
who_is_already_doing_this: ZeroPoint Technologies (CXL compression IP) [UNVERIFIED-T]; Marvell Structera (inline LZ4) [UNVERIFIED-T]; Intel IAA in Xeon + zswap (upstream); Meta TMO / Google zswap far-memory (software) [UNVERIFIED-T]; Rambus (CXL controller IP)
fatal_flaw: Compression is being absorbed for free into CPUs (Intel IAA + zswap, upstream) and merchant CXL controllers (inline LZ4). The hottest 'need more RAM' data, FP8/INT4 weights and KV, is near-incompressible, and FPGA BOM eats most of the saved DRAM value.
possible: yes: demonstrated on FPGA and in merchant controllers
profitable: no: squeezed between free CPU/controller compression and a glut

name: On-prem MoE Box (DRAM-instead-of-HBM inference appliance)
subbranch: HBM alternatives at system level: CPU-DRAM-resident MoE inference
wins_axis: $/GB of model-resident memory (DDR5 ~$26/GB vs ~$180-250/GB HBM-in-GPU) plus data sovereignty
buyer: 20-500-person regulated firms (law, healthcare, CMMC/ITAR defense subcontractors) and universities running private chat/RAG/agents on 600B-1T-parameter MoE models
us_manufacturability: Assembled and tested in the U.S. (East Coast bench). CPUs/GPUs are TSMC and DDR5 is Korea/Taiwan (Micron Idaho from 2027). 'Assembled in USA' only, though TAA-compliant integration is feasible.
who_is_already_doing_this: Puget Systems, Exxact, Lambda, Bizon, Supermicro, Dell Pro Max/HPE; NVIDIA DGX Station GB300 (large coherent memory) [UNVERIFIED-T]; Apple Mac Studio (512 GB unified memory) [UNVERIFIED-T]; KTransformers community/Chinese appliance vendors [UNVERIFIED-T]
fatal_flaw: Commodity integration with thin hardware margin. NVIDIA DGX Station, Apple unified-memory machines and big OEMs can undercut, and ~20-45 tok/s single-stream throughput disappoints multi-user deployments. The only moat is service quality, and it is a reseller business, not a memory venture.
possible: yes: documented open-source configurations
profitable: marginal: yes only if a recurring support/model subscription attaches
doable_by_founder: yes: integration + software, startable with deposits

name: TB-Class CXL Node for EDA/Genomics/HANA
subbranch: CXL memory expansion - vertical large-memory appliance
wins_axis: TB per socket and $/TB vs 4-socket servers or cloud high-memory instances
buyer: EDA teams at fabless startups, genomics cores, SAP HANA operators
us_manufacturability: U.S. integration. The CMM modules are Samsung/SK hynix (Korea) and Micron (non-U.S. assembly [UNVERIFIED-T]).
who_is_already_doing_this: Supermicro, Dell, HPE, Lenovo (CXL-ready platforms); Penguin Solutions/SMART Modular; Colfax, Silicon Mechanics; AWS/Azure high-memory instances [UNVERIFIED-T]
fatal_flaw: Big OEMs already sell CXL-ready platforms with the same modules. At 2026 DRAM prices the binding constraint is dollars, not slots, so breaking the CXL ceiling is not the customer's pain point.
possible: yes
profitable: marginal: VAR margins against OEM incumbents

name: Rack-Scale CXL Pooling Appliance
wins_axis: Stranded-memory reduction (fleet $/GB)
buyer: Hyperscale and large VM cloud operators
us_manufacturability: Switch/controller silicon from TSMC; chassis assembly could be U.S.
who_is_already_doing_this: Liqid (composable memory), GigaIO, XConn, Panmnesia (CXL 3.x switch), Unifabrix (status unknown), H3 Platform, Astera Labs, Enfabrica (NVIDIA acqui-hire Sep 2025) [all UNVERIFIED-T]
fatal_flaw: The OS is not ready: mainline Linux (2026-10-31) still lists Dynamic Capacity, multi-host sharing and fabrics as [0] known gaps. The only buyers big enough to benefit build their own, and Pond's own result was single-digit-percent savings.
possible: marginal: hardware exists, OS/pooling stack immature in late 2026
profitable: no

name: Persistent CXL Log Card (post-Optane PMem for WAL/journals)
subbranch: Tiered memory - persistent CXL tier (NVDIMM-N/MRAM successor)
wins_axis: Non-volatility at memory latency (durable commit latency)
buyer: Database vendors (log/commit path), storage-array OEMs (journals), low-latency trading
us_manufacturability: Board assembly U.S.; Everspin Toggle MRAM is made in Chandler AZ (STT 1Gb via GF Singapore); DRAM/NAND imported
who_is_already_doing_this: SMART Modular (CXL NV-CMM) [UNVERIFIED-T]; Samsung CMM-H (DRAM+NAND hybrid) [UNVERIFIED-T]; Netlist (NVDIMM history); Everspin (MRAM in IBM FCM); Kioxia XL-Flash
fatal_flaw: The market is tiny. Optane PMem died for lack of volume (>$7B losses). NVMe with power-loss protection plus group commit is 'good enough', and storage OEMs build journals in-house (IBM uses MRAM). MRAM at ~$821/GB caps capacity to megabytes-gigabytes.
possible: yes: NVDIMM-N and CXL NV-CMM demos exist
profitable: marginal: niche volumes

name: LPDDR 'HBM-lite' Memory Chiplet (UCIe/AIB-attached)
wins_axis: Bandwidth per dollar and allocation-free supply vs HBM for inference ASICs
buyer: AI-inference ASIC startups, edge-AI SoC teams, defense ASIC programs
us_manufacturability: GlobalFoundries Malta NY can fab a 12nm-class controller. Advanced packaging at Amkor Arizona (2027-28 [UNVERIFIED-T]). LPDDR5X dies are imported.
who_is_already_doing_this: Eliyan (NuLink die-to-die PHY), Marvell (custom HBM/memory chiplets), Synopsys/Cadence (UCIe + LPDDR IP), Alphawave (Qualcomm), d-Matrix, Tenstorrent, Primemas, NVIDIA Grace LPDDR5X [UNVERIFIED-T for company specifics]
fatal_flaw: IP giants (Synopsys, Cadence, Alphawave, Eliyan) already sell UCIe+LPDDR PHY/controller IP, and serious ASIC teams integrate in-house. A startup chiplet faces a $20-60M tape-out for a handful of customers.
possible: yes
profitable: marginal: crowded IP market

name: High-Bandwidth Flash (HBF) Weight-Store Module
subbranch: HBM alternatives - stacked NAND with HBM-like interface
wins_axis: Capacity per package and $/GB vs HBM for read-heavy inference weights
buyer: GPU/ASIC vendors (NVIDIA, AMD, hyperscaler ASIC teams)
us_manufacturability: None: NAND fabs in Japan, packaging in Asia; integration would happen inside GPU/ASIC packages at TSMC CoWoS.
who_is_already_doing_this: SanDisk (HBF, announced 2025 [UNVERIFIED-T]); SK hynix (HBF standardization MoU with SanDisk, Aug 2025 [UNVERIFIED-T]); Samsung, Kioxia (reported)
fatal_flaw: Integration happens inside GPU/ASIC packages at TSMC, so there is no socket for a small company. NAND endurance rules out write-heavy KV, so HBF is a weights-only niche controlled by memory makers and GPU vendors.
possible: marginal: TRL 4-5, samples not yet public
profitable: no for a small entrant

name: PIM DIMM Accelerator Servers (UPMEM / AiM) for Scans and Genomics
wins_axis: Throughput and energy per byte moved for memory-bound kernels
buyer: Genomics cores, analytics/database operators
us_manufacturability: None for PIM silicon (foreign DRAM-process partners); U.S. integration only
who_is_already_doing_this: UPMEM (France; current company status not verified this session); Samsung (HBM-PIM, LPDDR5X-PIM); SK hynix (GDDR6-AiM, AiMX); NeuroBlade (SQL accelerator); GSI Technology (SRAM APU, Sunnyvale) [UNVERIFIED-T]
fatal_flaw: Hard programming model, single-vendor supply risk, and DDR4-based UPMEM DIMMs stranded as servers go DDR5-only. GPUs with HBM run the same kernels with a mature CUDA stack.
possible: yes: real hardware characterized
profitable: no: no commercial pull beyond research

name: Analog CIM Edge Module (DRAM-free defense edge inference)
wins_axis: W per inference and a DRAM-free BOM at the edge
buyer: Defense UAS/ISR integrators, industrial machine vision
us_manufacturability: CIM chips designed in the U.S. (EnCharge Santa Clara, Mythic Austin), fabbed at TSMC/foreign foundries [UNVERIFIED-T]; module assembly U.S.
who_is_already_doing_this: EnCharge AI, Mythic, Sagence AI, IBM Research (analog AI), d-Matrix (digital IMC, datacenter), Axelera (EU); digital competitors Hailo, NVIDIA Jetson, Qualcomm [UNVERIFIED-T]
fatal_flaw: Edge AI is being won by digital NPUs with mature toolchains. Analog CIM carries accuracy/toolchain risk (IBM's kit is still 'beta') and startup-vendor fragility, and an integrator sits between two stronger parties: not a memory business.

who_is_already_doing_this: TrendForce (free press releases), Mobius Materials and BuySellRAM (free lead-gen reports), Tom's Hardware, Igor'sLAB, Objective Analysis (Jim Handy), SemiAnalysis and Fabricated Knowledge (paid) [UNVERIFIED-T].
fatal_flaw: It has no proprietary data or insider expertise against SemiAnalysis-class analysts and free vendor reports, and the realistic ceiling is a few thousand dollars of MRR.
possible: yes
profitable: marginal - side income, cyclical

name: Embedded RAM-Diet Profiler for Small Hardware OEMs
wins_axis: $/unit BOM (fewer GB of DRAM per device)
buyer: Hardware product managers at U.S. industrial, IoT and medical-device OEMs shipping 5k-200k units/year
us_manufacturability: Software and services; customers are U.S. industrial, IoT and medical OEMs and their SoM vendors.
who_is_already_doing_this: Embedded consultancies (Bootlin, Witekio, Toradex services) [UNVERIFIED-T], SoM vendor application engineers, Yocto buildhistory and smem (free), device-observability SaaS (Memfault [UNVERIFIED-T]).
fatal_flaw: Dropping a density step means board re-spin, re-qualification and (for medical) regulatory re-validation that cost more than a year of savings. Embedded engineers decide, and they rarely buy SaaS from non-engineers.
possible: yes - standard footprint tooling
profitable: marginal - lumpy consulting that dies in a glut

name: DIMM Health Subscription: predictive replacement + recovered-DDR4 spares pool
subbranch: SaaS + spares pool (third-party maintenance for memory only)
wins_axis: lifecycle length: $/GB-month of keeping installed DDR4 capacity running vs. refreshing at ~$20/GB DDR5
buyer: Operators of out-of-warranty DDR4 fleets: university research computing, regional colos and MSPs, on-prem SaaS/fintech shops. Also TPM providers as wholesale buyers of the prediction feed plus spares.
us_manufacturability: No fabrication. U.S. value-add is burn-in test of recovered RDIMMs on owned DDR4 server beds (memtest86+, stressapptest) in a small East Coast space, plus the software. Supply comes from U.S. R2/e-Stewards ITADs.
who_is_already_doing_this: Third-party maintenance firms bundle DIMM replacement into whole-server contracts (Park Place Technologies/Curvature, Service Express [UNVERIFIED-training]). Hyperscalers retire DIMMs on error trends in-house. OEM support (Dell ProSupport, HPE) covers in-warranty fleets. No memory-only predictive subscription was found, but a web search was not possible this session [UNVERIFIED].
fatal_flaw: Low spend per customer and bundling. DIMMs are a small slice of whole-server TPM contracts, so Park Place or Service Express can match it at no extra charge. Self-maintaining shops may just keep a box of spare DIMMs. The predictive layer is copyable from open-source rasdaemon.
possible: yes - every component exists (EDAC telemetry, recovered RDIMMs, NBD shipping)
profitable: marginal - 59-82% GM but ~$22k ACV; needs ~25+ customers for ~$0.5M ARR, and TPM bundling caps price
doable_by_founder: yes - T0, software-led, part-time start; first customers are reachable regionally

name: Memory Cost Escalation Index + EPA clause kit
wins_axis: contract-risk transfer: lower price contingency (cost certainty) on memory-heavy fixed-price contracts
buyer: U.S. system integrators and federal IT contractors on multi-year fixed-price deliveries (servers, rugged computers), regional and tier-2 EMS houses, industrial-PC OEMs (Advantech/OnLogic class) and their procurement counterparts.
us_manufacturability: Pure software/data; no fab dependency.
who_is_already_doing_this: TrendForce/DRAMeXchange (public spot board plus paid contract data), InSpectrum, TechInsights and Omdia sell the data. Free retail trackers exist. No memory-specific escalation-clause/index-licensing product was found [UNVERIFIED: search unavailable]. Closest analogues are metals surcharge indexes (CRU, Fastmarkets/AMM) [UNVERIFIED-training].
fatal_flaw: Credibility. Counterparties default to TrendForce/DRAMeXchange as the reference, and an index built from distributor list quotes rather than transactions is easy to dismiss or game. Licensing real contract data for redistribution may cost more than early revenue.
possible: yes - distributor APIs and index methodology are standard
profitable: marginal - high GM, but ~$0.3M ARR ceiling unless it becomes the reference index
doable_by_founder: yes - T0, part-time; the founder's day job (manufacturing ops) is the buyer persona

name: DRAM futures/swap market (index-settled forwards) - tempting, dead
wins_axis: price-risk transfer (cost certainty)
buyer: PC/phone OEMs, tier-2 clouds without LTAs, module makers (Kingston, ADATA class); second-tier DRAM makers (Nanya, Winbond) as natural sellers.
us_manufacturability: Financial product; no manufacturing. Would run on a U.S. CFTC-registered DCM/SEF or through a registered swap dealer.
who_is_already_doing_this: No listed DRAM futures are known on CME, ICE, SGX or TAIFEX [UNVERIFIED-training; could not search]. The de facto hedge is physical LTAs with prepayments (SK hynix: 14 LTAs, booked to 2029; CSP multi-year deals). Mobius Materials runs a physical spot marketplace.
fatal_flaw: No settlement-grade, licensable, manipulation-resistant index exists. TrendForce contract data is proprietary and survey-based, and spot is thin and panic-priced at ~1.7x contract. The big players already hedge physically through LTAs that simply re-price (Nanya +60%), so nobody supplies liquidity. CFTC registration and clearing push it to T3.
possible: marginal - the instrument type is standard, but the index and liquidity do not exist
profitable: no - no fee revenue until liquidity; physical LTAs are the entrenched substitute

name: DRAM price-cap / allocation-guarantee subscription ('memory insurance') - dead
wins_axis: cost certainty / supply security
buyer: SMB hardware OEMs, system integrators and tier-2 clouds without LTAs
us_manufacturability: Financial product; none.
who_is_already_doing_this: No DRAM price-cap product was found [UNVERIFIED: search unavailable]. Market substitutes are LTAs with prepayment and distributor allocation programs.
fatal_flaw: The venture is short a call option. The fair premium for an at-the-money 12-month cap is ~17-21% of capped spend (Black-76, 44-55% vol; e_estimates §2), which buyers will not pay. A 99th-percentile year costs the writer $1.5-2.1M per $1M of capped spend. Structured as indemnity it falls under state insurance regulation; structured as a price swap it falls under CFTC swap rules.
possible: marginal - structurally possible through a reinsurer, but no one will write it at a price buyers accept
profitable: no - adverse selection plus fat-tailed price moves

name: Buy-and-hold DRAM inventory arbitrage - speculation, not a venture
wins_axis: none (timing speculation)
buyer: whoever is short that day: brokers, CMs, system builders
us_manufacturability: None: storage only.
who_is_already_doing_this: Independent brokers and traders worldwide; Mobius Materials (VA) as a marketplace. Module makers' real business is already inventory timing (p1-backend).
fatal_flaw: A newcomer can only buy at spot (~$27/GB, ~1.7x contract) because makers allocate contract supply to strategic customers. The QoQ rate has slowed from +95% to +12.5%, so the expected 12-month net return is -46% (-22% even if the spot premium persists; e_estimates §3). Only allocation holders buying at contract see ~+7%. It is speculation with no recurring revenue and no moat.
possible: yes - anyone can buy spot inventory
profitable: no - negative expected value at spot; positive only for holders of contract allocation

name: DIMM leasing / memory-as-a-service financing for neoclouds
wins_axis: $/GB-month and cash-flow timing (no capex at peak prices)
buyer: neoclouds and AI-inference startups, mid-size enterprises without memory LTAs
us_manufacturability: None; financing. Modules are made in Asia or assembled in the U.S. by Kingston/Penguin from foreign die.
who_is_already_doing_this: OEM captive finance (Dell Financial Services, HPE Financial Services), IT lessors, GPU-backed lenders to neoclouds [UNVERIFIED-training].
fatal_flaw: Residual-value and counterparty risk both sit on the cycle: the lessor is long DRAM bought at peak prices and short credit on neoclouds. OEM captives with cheaper capital already lease whole servers, memory included.
possible: yes - IT leasing is mature
profitable: no - for a small lessor buying at 2026 prices into a 2028 glut

name: Authorized-aftermarket die bank for EOL legacy DRAM (title-taking LTB aggregator)
wins_axis: lifecycle length and supply security: authorized, traceable legacy DRAM after EOL
buyer: DoD sustainment programs and DMSMS offices, avionics (DO-254), rail signaling, medical-device OEMs
us_manufacturability: Die from Taiwan (or Micron Manassas if it ever sells die). Banking, packaging and test in the U.S. at Micross FL/NC, QP Technologies CA or Integra KS [UNVERIFIED-training sites].
who_is_already_doing_this: Rochester Electronics (Newburyport MA; authorized aftermarket for 70+ OCMs [UNVERIFIED-training]), Micross (largest authorized die supplier), Alliance Memory (long-lifecycle brand), distributors' bonded stock.
fatal_flaw: OCMs grant aftermarket authorization to proven firms with capital and quality systems (Rochester, Micross). A startup can neither win the authorization nor fund $2M+ of inventory, and without it the venture is just an independent distributor, which DFARS ranks last.
possible: yes - Rochester and Micross prove the model
profitable: yes - for incumbents with authorization and scale
doable_by_founder: no - capital, authorization and relationships are the moat

name: AS6171 counterfeit-detection and authentication lab for memory lots
wins_axis: supply security / authenticity (counterfeit-risk reduction with documentation)
buyer: AS6081 independent distributors, defense EMS and primes' purchasing departments, OEMs buying broker DRAM during the shortage
us_manufacturability: U.S. lab services; no fab.
who_is_already_doing_this: Established independent AS6171 labs and distributors' in-house labs (e.g., SMT Corp, Integra Technologies, Alter Technology [UNVERIFIED-training]); the ERAI/GIDEP reporting ecosystem; Mobius Materials' ML authentication.
fatal_flaw: A crowded, accreditation-heavy services market with entrenched labs. Below ~36 lots/month the lab loses money, and the founder cannot run it without a hired AS6171 test engineer and ~$650k.
possible: yes - routine lab methods
profitable: marginal - breakeven at ~36 lots/month; 41% GM at 60
doable_by_founder: marginal - needs a technical hire and ~$0.65M

name: 'Compliant memory' federal reseller on GSA MAS / SEWP (compliance-as-a-product)
wins_axis: supply security / compliance documentation
buyer: federal civilian and DoD IT buyers; prime integrators
us_manufacturability: Resale only; modules may be U.S.-assembled (Kingston, Penguin) from foreign die.
who_is_already_doing_this: Hundreds of federal IT VARs and SEWP holders (CDW-G, Carahsoft, many small businesses) [UNVERIFIED-training]; Micron and Kingston through their channels.
fatal_flaw: No pricing power. Above $174k, TAA lets Korean, Taiwanese and Japanese memory compete equally (FAR 25.402); the BAA component test is waived for COTS (FAR 25.001); and §5949 rewards 'not Chinese', which every Samsung, SK hynix or Micron reseller already meets. Neither the FAR (through FAC 2025-06) nor the DFARS (June 2026 snapshot) yet contains any §5949 text, and the §889 precedent accepts a 'reasonable inquiry' that excludes third-party audits (FAR 4.2101). Compliance is a free checkbox, leaving a 6-10% VAR margin on $1.5-2.5M of sales per $150k of gross profit (e_estimates §7).
possible: yes - standard VAR model
profitable: no - commodity margin; compliance confers no premium
doable_by_founder: marginal - slow vehicle access, working capital ~$185-310k

name: STTR vehicle on a national-lab / university memory patent (lab-patent studio)
subbranch: University/lab patent license -> STTR -> defense Phase III
wins_axis: non-volatility plus radiation/temperature tolerance (supply security for space and hypersonics)
buyer: AFRL/DARPA program offices, space primes, hypersonic and Venus/geothermal sensor integrators
us_manufacturability: Sandia MESA (trusted, but a government fab not open for production); SkyWater S130 / Fab 25 for a commercial path. Bayh-Dole and DOE U.S.-manufacture preferences align with U.S. production.
who_is_already_doing_this: C-06 (Sandia HZO FeRAM chip) and C-07 (AlScN license plus STTR) card the device plays. Incumbents: Infineon rad-hard F-RAM, Frontgrade/Everspin Toggle MRAM. Many university spinouts run this STTR pattern.
fatal_flaw: It is the grant farm the founder says he does not want. The chance of customer revenue is ~3% per topic attempt and ~15% after five (e_estimates §8). First revenue lands ~46 months out, past the 36-month ceiling. The vehicle depends on a lab PI and a fab it does not control. Tech-transfer listings and patent numbers could not be verified this session.
possible: yes - option/STTR/Phase III mechanics are routine; device TRL 3-5
profitable: marginal - niche defense NVM can be profitable for whoever reaches Phase III, rarely within 4 years
doable_by_founder: marginal - he can run the company shell and proposals, not the science

name: SBA/search-fund acquisition of a small memory reseller at peak earnings - tempting, dangerous
wins_axis: time-to-revenue (acquired), not a product axis
buyer: the target's existing customers: SMB IT, refurbishers, MSPs, homelab/gaming buyers
us_manufacturability: Existing U.S. operation (testing and resale); no fab.
who_is_already_doing_this: Search funds and ETA buyers generally; ITAD consolidators such as Iron Mountain ALM (ITRenew) [UNVERIFIED-training].
fatal_flaw: Buying cyclical peak earnings with leverage. Shortage-inflated EBITDA reverts, and the SBA personal guarantee ties the founder's personal assets to the 2028 glut.
possible: yes - SBA acquisitions of small distributors are routine
profitable: no - at 2026 prices; maybe yes if bought in the trough
doable_by_founder: no - equity gap and guarantee risk

name: Acquire the 3D XPoint/Optane IP estate and license it (business-model Optane revival) - tempting, dead
wins_axis: $/GB vs. DRAM plus persistence
buyer: CXL memory-tier buyers (hyperscalers, SAP HANA/database hosts)
us_manufacturability: No XPoint line exists anywhere: Lehi was sold to TI and converted to 65/45nm analog.
who_is_already_doing_this: Nobody. SanDisk's 3D-matrix/HBF work and imec research are the nearest descendants (see C-25, C-25, C-53).
fatal_flaw: IP without a line is worthless. No fab runs XPoint and rebuilding one is T3-T4. Micron and Intel both exited (Micron cited 'insufficient market validation'), and out-licensing memory IP takes a decade even for the best-run licensor (Weebit is still sub-scale).
possible: marginal - the IP could be bought; the product cannot be made without a new line
profitable: no
